Let's fat tax airline tickets - Jerusalem Post

Although this sounds like a great idea, I see some problems with the logistics.

  1. Most people save up and prepay for their trips. If those people were to arrive at the airport expecting to pay $500 and their weight increases the cost to $800 you're going to have a lot of people who will be unable to come up with the extra $300 and will be forced to forgo their flight. This costs the airlines money because they had reserved a seat for an standard person expecting them to pay $500 for the seat and now they're getting $0. I think a solution to this would be to set the standard cost to a higher level and offer refunds for those people who weigh less than expected. I do like the idea of allowing smaller people a free checked bag.

  2. People who are weighed at the airport by an airline employee are going to be angry or humiliated if they are overweight and may take that anger out on the airline by never selecting it again when flying. We could make this all automated and private, but I think people will still punish the airline for pointing out that they're overweight.

  3. Checking in and boarding for a flight is nightmarish already, do we really want to add another level of bureaucracy and another reason for people to be manhandled?

So eventually one airline will be virtually free of extra space hogging passengers? Sounds like a selling point.
What happens when you have an entire plane load of people that are well overweight?

Unfortunately, most of the US population is overweight, and that includes children. If you take a domestic flight in the US chances are that more than half of the travelers are overweight to some degree. The real cost in air travel comes down to fuel. It takes more fuel to move greater mass across the same distance. I think it would be more fair to pay your actual share of the cost instead of subsidizing people who are taking up more space than others and causing more fuel to be consumed than if all the passengers were of a healthy weight.
how much weight can you unwittingly gain in 2-3 months time? Besides the surcharge isn't likely to be that high - see: baggage fees, usualy $25-$50 extra.

I think that most people aren't aware of their actual weight. They seem to be in denial about their problem, so I see it going something like this: "The jeans I'm wearing are a size 22. When I last weighed myself I wore a 22, therefore I am the same weight." totally disregarding the fact that vanity sizing is making them think they wear a smaller size than they would in clothing from 10 or 20 years ago. Also, manufacturer to manufacturer the sizes will differ. Weighing themselves would require them facing the fact that they're overweight, and they don't want to believe that because it would mean that they let themselves get fat, and that is too difficult to accept for most people. It's easier to pretend that nothing is wrong than to face your shortcomings.

I know a woman who would shop around various stores and would select clothing based on size. If it had a tag that said size 4 and she could fit in it, she would wear it, and then show everyone, "See, I'm skinny, I'm a size 4" The problem is that in most clothing lines she was a size 8, but she wanted to believe that she was thin, so she went to great lengths to prove to herself, and her friends, that she was "still" a size 4, even though she'd put on 30 pounds in the past 10 years.

1) the cost would be known in advance; when you check the price of a ticket you would simply input your weight and the price is calculated.. Basically, that's the way freight works. As far as the plane it's concerned, people are just cargo.

2) Okay, then the airline would eventually have to stop charging or go bankrupt. This isn't a reason to not try it. I think the exact opposite would happen. The airline would be overbooked with lighter, thinner people trying to ensure they have the most comfortable flight possible.

3) It wouldn't really add much to the process. It takes about ten seconds for a scale to register. Just compare that with weight that was only when the ticket was purchased online to make sure the correct price has been charged.

I agree with another poster that you should break the pricing into tiers to simplify things. Would be similar to baggage.

Another idea is to have a gadget like the one that measures baggage. If you can't fit through it then you have to purchase business or a second seat. In wondering if airlines might have to add a row or two of larger economy seats reserved for the obese. Economy service but base price based on the number of seats displaced, plus weight addition.

At this point I don't think it's " if" but "when" the major airlines start doing something. Fuel isn't free and more weight equals more burned fuel.

There could also be some positive effects. After all, for people who fly a few times per year, and companies that fly employees constantly there is now a financial incentive to lose weight or pay your employees to lose weight.

I really don't see many negatives.
